summary_of_threads_started_this_week:
The recent discussions from various mailing lists reveal significant advancements and considerations in blockchain technology and cryptocurrency frameworks. A novel Layer 2 (L2) transaction system proposed by Adam Gibson and detailed in the [Lichen Draft Paper](https://github.com/AdamISZ/lichen/blob/master/papers/lichen-draft.pdf) allows for secure, co-owned contract transactions on the Bitcoin blockchain without requiring trust in a central hub's honesty. This system leverages multi-signature setups and cryptographic proofs to ensure user control over funds even if the hub goes offline, potentially expanding to support complex smart contracts and high-privacy transactions.

Luke Carriere has introduced a draft to standardize enforcement policies for blockchain co-signers, aiming to enhance interoperability across different security products like Liquidium and Lendasat. This draft, outlined in [Draft BIP](https://github.com/lukecarriere/bip-cosigner-spending-policies/blob/main/bip-cosigner-spending-policies.md), suggests a unified format for various verification methods and conditions, fostering greater compatibility and security in co-signed transactions across diverse blockchain applications.

Furthermore, an emerging protocol named Cassis, as discussed at [Cassis](https://cassis.cash/), proposes a streamlined method for conducting payments across multiple blockchain layers using Hash Time Locked Contracts (HTLCs). This approach not only simplifies transaction routing via various solvers but also enhances user flexibility in managing privacy and security settings without sacrificing functionality. The ongoing development and challenges of this protocol are actively documented and accessible on [GitHub](https://github.com/cassiscash/cassi), inviting contributions to refine and optimize this innovative payment mechanism.

new_threads_this_week.title: Lichen: L2s In CHannels ENforced on bitcoin
new_threads_this_week.summary: - This L2 network system permits secure, trust-free interactions with a centralized hub.  - Disputed withdrawals on this platform utilize RISC Zero and a Groth16 verifier for resolution.  - The system maintains liquidity and supports advanced functionalities like high-privacy transactions.

new_threads_this_week.title: RE BIP 300: 26% censoring attack
new_threads_this_week.summary:
- Attackers can manipulate Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 300 scores using ALARM messages.
- Prohibiting ALARM messages could restore integrity to Bitcoin's 51% security assumption.
- Proposed changes enhance security and ensure fair transaction verifications.

new_threads_this_week.title: Anchoring an SPV light client on another chain: checkpoint trust, retargeting and reorg handling
new_threads_this_week.summary: - The Writz Protocol uses Bitcoin as collateral, disburses loans as USDC on Stellar.  - The protocol employs a Pay-to-Witness-Script-Hash output for security and conditional fund access.  - It is suggested to improve trust mechanisms and manage transaction fees and reorg limits.

new_threads_this_week.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
new_threads_this_week.summary:
- Luke Carriere's draft aims to standardize transaction co-signing policies, not co-signers.
- The proposal includes three verification types: open, blinded, and enclave verification.
- The BIP draft seeks feedback on data formats and verification processes to improve interoperability.

new_threads_this_week.title: Cassis, a new simple scheme for generic multi-layer multi-hop HTLC routing
new_threads_this_week.summary:
- Bitcoin's evolving payment ecosystem includes scalable solutions such as Arkade's Intents protocol.
- Kaleidoswap leverages HTLCs to enable generic frameworks for Bitcoin's multi-layered transactions.
- Cassis introduces a system linking HTLCs for reversible payments, enhancing privacy and security options.
